fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Paul says, "But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you." (2 Corinthians 8:16) Paul doesn't take credit for it. He thanks God. Titus, Paul's partner and fellow worker, has the very same devotion Paul has.

Nope, no worry in this verse, friend. Paul is thanking God here. What God put in Titus's heart was "…the same devotion I have for you." (2 Corinthians 8:16) That's devotion for the Corinthians, plain and simple.

Close, but it's true, baker. Paul says, "For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition." (2 Corinthians 8:17) Titus welcomed the appeal, and he is eagerly coming of his own volition too. So the statement holds.

Synagogue, friend? You're thinking religious work, and I respect that energy. But it isn't in the verse. Paul says this brother is praised by all the churches "…for his work in the gospel." (2 Corinthians 8:18) The gospel, the good news, is the answer.

Whoa, that's a different direction, friend. Paul says nothing about being paid in this verse. The offering is administered "…to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help." (2 Corinthians 8:19) Honoring the Lord and showing eagerness to help, that's what Paul says it's for.

Not here, baker. Paul says nothing about power over the churches. In this very verse, the churches chose this brother to travel with the team, and the offering is "…to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help." (2 Corinthians 8:19) That's honoring the Lord and showing eagerness.

Right on, baker. Paul says, "We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift." (2 Corinthians 8:20) He wants the gift handled so well that nobody has a complaint about it. That's careful work, and I like it.

Yes, false! Paul says, "For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men." (2 Corinthians 8:21) He cares about the Lord's eyes, and he cares about people's eyes too. Both count, and those two little words "not only" are the clue.

Paying his own way, baker? Nice try on the travel budget, but the text never says who covers the trip. Paul says this brother's earnestness shows "…now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) The proof is his confidence in the Corinthians.

Leaving home is a reasonable thought, friend, but the verse doesn't point there. Paul says this brother's earnestness shows "…now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) It's about what he believes of the Corinthians. His confidence in them is the answer.
Messengers, you got it, baker! Paul says, "As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ." (2 Corinthians 8:23) And what a title: the glory of Christ.

Rulers would be a big title, baker, but Paul doesn't use it. He says, "…they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ." (2 Corinthians 8:23) Messengers is the word he picked. Rulers isn't in the verse.

Yes, the proof of their love! Paul writes, "In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) That's what he asks the Corinthians to show, in full view of the churches. It's the second thing he names besides the reason for the boasting.

Respect for Paul's authority? I see why you'd go there, baker, but Paul doesn't ask for that here. He asks them to "…show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) Love is on his list. Authority isn't.

Courage under trial? Good thing to have, friend, but it's not in this verse. Paul asks the Corinthians to "…show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) Love is what he names, so love is the answer.

True, baker! Paul says, "Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you." (2 Corinthians 9:1) He says it because he knows their eagerness to help. The next verse spells that out.

That's it, baker. Paul says, "But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said." (2 Corinthians 9:3) He's been boasting about the Corinthians. He wants them prepared so that boasting holds up.

Checking on the teaching is a different job, friend, and it's not this one. Paul says he's sending the brothers "…in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said." (2 Corinthians 9:3) This trip is about being prepared to give. That's the answer.

Not quite, baker. Paul says, "…we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident." (2 Corinthians 9:4) The word "we" means Paul's team would be ashamed too. So it's false that only the Corinthians would be.

Yes, baker! Paul wants the brothers to "…make arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly." (2 Corinthians 9:5) The gift was already promised. He wants it prepared the right way, and generously is the word he uses.
